title: Refund Method by Cancellation Reason — Risk Premium and Reserve Fund Charges, NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## Risk premium and reserve fund assessment charges returned on cancellation (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))

The refund-method rule decides how much of the risk premium and reserve fund assessment charges is given back when a signed cancellation is processed:

| Reason or date | Risk premium and reserve fund assessment charges given back |
|---|---|
| Duplicate NFIP Policy or Closing Did Not Occur | The cancellation reaches back to the policy's inception: every such charge booked on the policy, net of its re-rate credits on earlier terms, is returned in full — the charges booked at the current term start together with every earlier term's charges on those two lines |
| Removed from SFHA by LOMA or LOMR, or a cancellation that takes effect on or before the current term start | The charges booked at the current term start are returned in full, because the current term then never ran |
| Any other reason, cancellation taking effect after the term start | Those charges are returned at the term share — the days from the cancellation date to the term end divided by the days of the current term |

*Hypothetical cases* (risk premium booked at the current term start 1,000.00 dollars; earlier terms' risk premium charges 900.00 with 50.00 of re-rate credits on those terms). Duplicate NFIP Policy: 1,850.00 given back on the risk premium line. Removed from SFHA by LOMA or LOMR: 1,000.00. Building Sold with 73 of 365 days left: 200.00.
